what_happened: On a multi-lane highway, the ego was going straight at about 5 m/s with a clear lane ahead, but its plan started veering left toward actor 37's lane. By 6.7 s it had cut across the lane line and its front hit actor 56, a car in the adjacent left lane. The recorded human car stayed in its lane (and the route command was turning RIGHT), and the camera looked clean before impact, so the bad lane change was the policy's own mistake.

The ego held about 8 m/s near its recorded path, within 0.8 m of where the human drove. Actor 33 came up quickly from behind in the lane to the left and drew alongside, and its right side met the ego's left front corner, which sat close to the lane line. Contact was side-to-side between two vehicles moving in parallel. The ego did not steer into actor 33 and could do little to avoid it. Actor 33 is a replayed vehicle that does not react to the ego, and the ego was slightly off the recording, so who is at fault is unclear.

After the policy took over in moderate highway traffic, it planned and steered a leftward drift into the next lane even though the command was STRAIGHT and later RIGHT. While speeding up to about 5.9 m/s it cut into actor 56, which was travelling in that left lane right beside it, and hit it with its front.

On a multi-lane freeway at about 8 m/s, the policy planned a lane change to the left and moved the ego about 0.9 m off the recorded path toward the left lane. Vehicle 33 was coming up alongside in that lane, and the ego's front corner hit it at 6.2 s; the camera smear on the left appears only at the moment of contact.

After handoff, the ego was on a multi-lane highway with the command STRAIGHT, later RIGHT. Its plan swung left toward the next lane while speeding up from 4.2 to 6.0 m/s, and it cut across into actor 56, which was travelling alongside it in the left lane, hitting it with its front at 6.7 s. The lead car was more than 20 m ahead and the camera view before impact was clean, so the unneeded lane change into an occupied lane caused the collision.

On a multi-lane highway at about 8 m/s with the command STRAIGHT, the policy took over at 4.6 s and planned a lane change to the left. It drifted toward the left lane, and actor 33, which was coming up alongside in that lane, was beside it. The ego's front-left corner hit actor 33 at 6.2 s.

With a RIGHT command, the ego stayed in the far-left lane, about 7–8 m left of the recorded path, which curves right. It slowed from 8.5 to 5.4 m/s, and its plan then bent left toward the median island, so it went off the drivable area at the island's edge. There was no collision; the smearing on the left of the camera image appears to come from the ego being far from where the real car drove, not to be what caused the mistake.

The ego was going about 4 m/s on a multi-lane highway and slowly drifted left, about 1.7 m off the recorded human path; its planned path also bent left. A small actor (id 19) passing on the left in the next lane clipped the ego's left side, and the simulator logged it as a lateral collision with the ego at fault.

While the ego was still replaying the logged trajectory before handoff (deviation 0 m, about 14 m/s), actor 16 came up from behind, overlapped the ego (rear collision flagged at 2.7–3.7 s, camera smeared inside the car) and ended up just ahead of it. At handoff (4.7 s), the ego's front bumper is still overlapping actor 16, so a front collision was registered at the very instant the policy took control, with no time for the policy to react.
